formulas.formula: A simple, clean budget: plan once, type what you spend each month, see where it goes.
Fills in from the year above (this year if blank).
To change it, select the money cells and use Format > Number.
1. Type your budget year below. Every tab follows it.
2. Open Categories. Type your income and how much you plan to spend in each category each month.
Rename the categories to fit your life; use the blank rows for more.
3. Each month, open that month's tab and type what you really spent in the Actual column.
4. The Budget column fills in from Categories. Different this month? Just type over it.
5. The Year Summary and Dashboard fill themselves in.
6. Tick your bills on Bills Checklist, and track goals and debt on their tabs.
7. The example numbers show a whole year. To start fresh, clear the Actual columns on the month tabs
and type over the other examples.
Your year at a glance: totals, charts and top categories.
Your income and spending categories, with a monthly budget for each.
One simple page per month: budget vs. actual, and what's left.
Every category, every month, with totals and averages.
Your bills with due days. Tick each one when it's paid.
Goals with progress bars, filled in from your savings.
Your debts and how much you've paid off.
Cream cells: these calculate for you.
Red: over budget, or something to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Keep it simple, keep it going.
Updates on its own from your month tabs.
Type your categories and a monthly budget for each. Rename them freely, but don't insert or delete rows.
Left to budget (income - bills - spending - savings)
Aim for $0 left to budget: every dollar has a job. Red = you planned more than you earn.
Tip for January: Start simple: a budget you keep beats a perfect one you drop.
Tip for February: Short month? Look for one category to trim, not ten.
Tip for March: Check your subscriptions: cancel one you don't use.
Tip for April: Tax refund or bonus? Give it a job before it lands.
Tip for May: Halfway through spring: compare this month with January.
Tip for June: Summer plans? Put a little in your vacation fund every month.
Tip for July: Midyear check: look at the Year Summary averages.
Tip for August: Back-to-school costs are coming: plan them now.
Tip for September: Fall is a good time to review insurance and phone plans.
Tip for October: Start your holiday gift list with a budget for each person.
Tip for November: Holiday sales: buy only what's already on your list.
Tip for December: Look back at your year on the Dashboard and set next year's budget.
Tick a box when a bill is paid. Paid (last column) = boxes ticked this year.
Tip: set due-date reminders on your phone for the bills you pay by hand.
Pick the Savings category you put money into for each goal. Saved This Year fills in from your month tabs.
Months to Go = what's left / your average monthly saving. One goal per category (red = used twice).
Once a month, type each debt's Current Balance from your statement.
Months Left is a rough guide: balance / payment, without interest.
